# sherpa-sparkline

A compact inline trend chart (line area or bars).

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Category | chart |
| Figma | Data Field |
| Source | [.ts](../../src/components/sherpa-sparkline/sherpa-sparkline.ts) · [.html](../../src/components/sherpa-sparkline/sherpa-sparkline.html) · [.css](../../src/components/sherpa-sparkline/sherpa-sparkline.css) · [.component.json](../../src/components/sherpa-sparkline/sherpa-sparkline.component.json) · [.example.json](../../src/components/sherpa-sparkline/sherpa-sparkline.example.json) |

## Example

```html
<sherpa-sparkline aria-label="Revenue, last 7 days"></sherpa-sparkline>
```

`populate()` is given, on `sherpa-sparkline`:

```json
[
  3,
  5,
  2,
  6,
  8,
  4,
  7
]
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-type` | `bar` |  | line (default, area + stroke) \| bar (flat-topped columns) |
| `data-values` | text |  | comma-separated or JSON array (e.g. "10,25,15,30") |

## Parts

Style these from outside with `::part()`:

`chart`, `hotspots`

## CSS custom properties it reads

What each class's base rule reads:

| Custom property | Class | Property |
|---|---|---|
| `--sherpa-display-mode-border-rounding-full` | `.point` | `border-radius` |
| `--sherpa-display-mode-size-sm` | `.hotspot` | `inline-size` |
| `--sherpa-display-mode-size-sm` | `.hotspot` | `block-size` |

## populate()

`number[]`

the points, kept in data-values, which is the source of truth
